steps.name: bills
steps.sql:
-- One bill or resolution in one Congress, from its Congress.gov bill-status record.
-- Status is the highest milestone among the record's action codes, in the
-- unitedstates/congress vocabulary. This covers the main milestones only; the
-- full status rules also read chamber, vote type and resolution kind.
SELECT
  lower(b.type_text) || b.number_text || '-' || b.congress_text AS bill_id,
  CAST(b.congress_text AS INTEGER) AS congress,
  lower(b.type_text) AS bill_type,
  CAST(b.number_text AS INTEGER) AS number,
  b.bill_title AS title,
  (regexp_match(b.sponsors, '<bioguideId>([^<]+)</bioguideId>'))[1] AS sponsor_person_id,
  CAST(b.introduced_date_text AS DATE) AS introduced_date,
  CAST(b.latest_action_date_text AS DATE) AS latest_action_date,
  (regexp_match(b.latest_action, '<text>([^<]*)</text>'))[1] AS latest_action,
  CASE
    WHEN b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>36000</actionCode>%'
      OR b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>E40000</actionCode>%' THEN 'ENACTED:SIGNED'
    WHEN b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>31000</actionCode>%' THEN 'PROV_KILL:VETO'
    WHEN b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>28000</actionCode>%' THEN 'PASSED:BILL'
    WHEN b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>8000</actionCode>%'
      AND b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>17000</actionCode>%' THEN 'PASSED:BILL'
    WHEN b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>8000</actionCode>%' THEN 'PASS_OVER:HOUSE'
    WHEN b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>17000</actionCode>%' THEN 'PASS_OVER:SENATE'
    WHEN b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>5000</actionCode>%'
      OR b.actions LIKE '%<actionCode>14000</actionCode>%' THEN 'REPORTED'
    ELSE 'INTRODUCED'
  END AS status,
  (regexp_match(b.actions, 'Became Public Law No: ([0-9]+-[0-9]+)'))[1] AS public_law_id
FROM bill_status AS b

steps.name: rulemaking_timeline
steps.sql:
-- One dated event in one rulemaking, from one source document.
-- A rulemaking is keyed by its RIN, or by its docket when the document names no RIN.
-- A Federal Register document is identified by its number and publication date: corrections reuse numbers.
-- DataFusion needs distinct names within every UNION branch, so repeated columns are aliased.
WITH fr AS (
  SELECT
    unnest(CASE WHEN array_length(d.regulation_id_numbers) > 0
                THEN d.regulation_id_numbers ELSE d.docket_ids END) AS rulemaking_id,
    d.document_number || '@' || d.publication_date AS source_key,
    d.document_number, d.title, d.type, d.publication_date, d.publication_date_typed,
    d.comments_close_on_typed, d.effective_on_typed
  FROM federal_register_documents AS d
),
regs AS (
  SELECT
    coalesce(json_get_str(k.attributes, 'rin'), d.attributes_docket_id) AS rulemaking_id,
    d.id, d.attributes_title AS title, json_get_str(d.attributes, 'frDocNum') AS fr_document_number,
    CAST(substr(json_get_str(d.attributes, 'commentStartDate'), 1, 10) AS DATE) AS opens,
    CAST(substr(json_get_str(d.attributes, 'commentEndDate'), 1, 10) AS DATE) AS closes
  FROM regulations_documents AS d
  LEFT JOIN regulations_dockets AS k ON k.id = d.attributes_docket_id
)
SELECT rulemaking_id,
       CASE type WHEN 'Proposed Rule' THEN 'proposed_rule' WHEN 'Rule' THEN 'final_rule' ELSE 'other' END AS event,
       source_key, publication_date_typed AS event_date, title,
       document_number AS fr_document_number, publication_date AS fr_publication_date,
       CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS regulations_document_id
FROM fr
UNION ALL
SELECT rulemaking_id, 'comment_period_closes', source_key, comments_close_on_typed, title,
       document_number AS fr_document_number, publication_date, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR)
FROM fr WHERE comments_close_on_typed IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT rulemaking_id, 'effective', source_key, effective_on_typed, title,
       document_number AS fr_document_number, publication_date, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR)
FROM fr WHERE effective_on_typed IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT rulemaking_id, 'comment_period_opens', id AS source_key, opens, title, fr_document_number, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR), id AS regulations_document_id
FROM regs WHERE opens IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT rulemaking_id, 'comment_period_closes', id AS source_key, closes, title, fr_document_number, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR), id AS regulations_document_id
FROM regs WHERE closes IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT a.rin_text, 'agenda_listing', a.rin_text || '@' || a.publication_publication_id_text,
       to_date(a.publication_publication_id_text || '01', '%Y%m%d'), a.rule_title_text,
       CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS fr_document_number, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS fr_publication_date,
       CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS regulations_document_id
FROM unified_agenda_entries AS a

steps.name: docket_comments
steps.sql:
-- One Regulations.gov docket, with totals of its public comments.
WITH comments AS (
  SELECT c.id, c.attributes_docket_id AS docket_id,
         coalesce(c.attributes_duplicate_comments, 0) AS duplicates,
         CAST(c.attributes_posted_date_typed AS DATE) AS posted
  FROM regulations_comments AS c
  WHERE c.attributes_docket_id IS NOT NULL
),
totals AS (
  SELECT docket_id, count(*) AS comments_posted, count(*) + sum(duplicates) AS comments_received,
         min(posted) AS first_posted, max(posted) AS last_posted
  FROM comments
  GROUP BY docket_id
),
docket_rulemakings AS (
  -- A docket can be named by more than one rulemaking; keep one so the docket stays one row.
  SELECT docket_id, min(rulemaking_id) AS rulemaking_id, min(agency_organization_id) AS agency_organization_id
  FROM (SELECT unnest(r.docket_ids) AS docket_id, r.rulemaking_id, r.agency_organization_id
        FROM rulemakings AS r) AS named
  GROUP BY docket_id
),
commenting_organizations AS (
  SELECT c.docket_id, count(DISTINCT o.organization_id) AS organizations
  FROM comments AS c
  JOIN entity_matches AS m
    ON m.left_scheme = 'regulations_gov_comment' AND m.left_id = c.id
   AND m.entity_kind = 'organization' AND m.decision = 'same'
  JOIN organizations AS o ON o.organization_id = m.right_id
  GROUP BY c.docket_id
),
campaigns AS (
  SELECT docket_id, sum(comments) AS comments
  FROM comment_campaigns
  WHERE comments > 1
  GROUP BY docket_id
)
SELECT t.docket_id, r.rulemaking_id, r.agency_organization_id,
       t.comments_posted, t.comments_received,
       coalesce(o.organizations, 0) AS organizations_commenting,
       coalesce(k.comments, 0) AS campaign_comments,
       t.first_posted, t.last_posted
FROM totals AS t
LEFT JOIN docket_rulemakings AS r ON r.docket_id = t.docket_id
LEFT JOIN commenting_organizations AS o ON o.docket_id = t.docket_id
LEFT JOIN campaigns AS k ON k.docket_id = t.docket_id

steps.name: open_comment_periods
steps.sql:
-- What can I comment on right now?
SELECT r.rulemaking_id, r.title, r.agency_organization_id, t.event_date AS comments_close, t.regulations_document_id
FROM rulemaking_timeline AS t
JOIN rulemakings AS r ON r.rulemaking_id = t.rulemaking_id
WHERE t.event = 'comment_period_closes' AND t.event_date >= CAST($1 AS DATE)
ORDER BY t.event_date, r.rulemaking_id

steps.name: member_voting_record
steps.sql:
-- How did this member vote?
SELECT c.vote_date, c.chamber, c.question, c.result, c.bill_id, v.vote, v.vote_as_recorded
FROM member_votes AS v
JOIN roll_calls AS c ON c.roll_call_id = v.roll_call_id
WHERE v.person_id = $1
ORDER BY c.vote_date DESC, c.roll_call_id

steps.name: rule_history
steps.sql:
-- What happened to this rule, and when?
SELECT event_date, event, title, fr_document_number, regulations_document_id
FROM rulemaking_timeline
WHERE rulemaking_id = $1
ORDER BY event_date, event, source_key

queries.name: bills_grain
queries.sql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT bill_id FROM bills GROUP BY bill_id HAVING count(*) > 1)) AS duplicate_keys, (SELECT count(*) FROM bills WHERE bill_id IS NULL) AS null_keys, (SELECT count(*) FROM bills) AS row_count

queries.name: rulemaking_timeline_grain
queries.sql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT rulemaking_id, event, source_key FROM rulemaking_timeline GROUP BY rulemaking_id, event, source_key HAVING count(*) > 1)) AS duplicate_keys, (SELECT count(*) FROM rulemaking_timeline WHERE rulemaking_id IS NULL OR event IS NULL OR source_key IS NULL) AS null_keys, (SELECT count(*) FROM rulemaking_timeline) AS row_count

queries.name: docket_comments_grain
queries.sql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT docket_id FROM docket_comments GROUP BY docket_id HAVING count(*) > 1)) AS duplicate_keys, (SELECT count(*) FROM docket_comments WHERE docket_id IS NULL) AS null_keys, (SELECT count(*) FROM docket_comments) AS row_count

queries.name: open_comment_periods_rows
queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS row_count FROM open_comment_periods

queries.name: member_voting_record_rows
queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS row_count FROM member_voting_record

queries.name: rule_history_rows
queries.sql: SELECT count(*) AS row_count FROM rule_history
